67683-the-boys-book-of-model-aeroplanes-.title: Flying Machine
67683-the-boys-book-of-model-aeroplanes-.creator: Francis A. Collins
67683-the-boys-book-of-model-aeroplanes-.description: A book by Francis A. Collins. In the boy’s calendar nowadays the aëroplane season comes in with sledding and runs all through skating, marble, top, kite-flying, and bicycle time. The delights of all the old games seem to be found in this marvelous new toy. The fun in throwing a top cannot compare with that of launching an aëroplane, while kite-flying is a very poor substitute for the actual conquest of the air.

arxiv-2007-00478.title: PAD-UFES-20: a skin lesion dataset composed of patient data and clinical images collected from smartphones
arxiv-2007-00478.creator: Andre G. C. Pacheco, Gustavo R. Lima, Amanda S. Salomão, Breno A. Krohling, Igor P. Biral, Gabriel G. de Angelo, Fábio C. R. Alves Jr, José G. M. Esgario, Alana C. Simora, Pedro B. C. Castro, Felipe B. Rodrigues, Patricia H. L. Frasson, Renato A. Krohling, Helder Knidel, Maria C. S. Santos, Rachel B
arxiv-2007-00478.description: Abstract Over the past few years, different computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) systems have been proposed to tackle skin lesion analysis. Most of these systems work only for dermoscopy images since there is a strong lack of public clinical images archive available to design them.

arxiv-2102-04287.title: Operation is the hardest teacher: estimating DNN accuracy looking for mispredictions Thanks: This work has been supported by the project COSMIC of UNINA DIETI.
arxiv-2102-04287.creator: Antonio Guerriero, Roberto Pietrantuono, Stefano Russo
arxiv-2102-04287.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Antonio Guerriero, Roberto Pietrantuono, Stefano Russo. Deep Neural Networks (DNN) are typically tested for accuracy relying on a set of unlabelled real world data (operational dataset), from which a subset is selected, manually labelled and used as test suite. This subset is required to be small (due to manual labelling cost) yet to faithfully represent the operational context, with the resulting test suite containing roughly the same proportion of examples causing misprediction (i.e., failing test cases) as the operational dataset.

arxiv-2203-01974.title: Towards Rich, Portable, and Large-Scale Pedestrian Data Collection*
arxiv-2203-01974.creator: Allan Wang, Abhijat Biswas, Henny Admoni, Aaron Steinfeld
arxiv-2203-01974.description: Abstract Recently, pedestrian behavior research has shifted towards machine learning based methods and converged on the topic of modeling pedestrian interactions. For this, a large-scale dataset that contains rich information is needed. We propose a data collection system that is portable, which facilitates accessible large-scale data collection in diverse environments.

arxiv-2211-09812.title: GAMMT: Generative Ambiguity Modeling Using Multiple Transformers
arxiv-2211-09812.creator: Xingcheng Xu
arxiv-2211-09812.description: Abstract We introduce a novel model called GAMMT (Generative Ambiguity Models using Multiple Transformers) for sequential data that is based on sets of probabilities. Unlike conventional models, our approach acknowledges that the data generation process of a sequence is not deterministic, but rather ambiguous and influenced by a set of probabilities.

arxiv-2303-08792.title: Building an Effective Email Spam Classification Model with spaCy
arxiv-2303-08792.creator: Kazem Taghandiki 1
arxiv-2303-08792.description: Abstract Today, people use email services such as Gmail, Outlook, AOL Mail, etc. to communicate with each other as quickly as possible to send information and official letters. Spam or junk mail is a major challenge to this type of communication, usually sent by botnets with the aim of advertising, harming and stealing information in bulk to different people.

arxiv-2402-14287.title: Tropical Fermat-Weber Polytropes
arxiv-2402-14287.creator: John Sabol, David Barnhill, Ruriko Yoshida, Keiji Miura
arxiv-2402-14287.description: Abstract We study the geometry of tropical Fermat-Weber points in terms of the symmetric tropical metric over the tropical projective torus. It is well-known that a tropical Fermat-Weber point of a given sample is not unique and we show that the set of all possible Fermat-Weber points forms a polytrope.

arxiv-2502-21242.title: Towards long-term player tracking with graph hierarchies and domain-specific features
arxiv-2502-21242.creator: Maria Koshkina, James H. Elder
arxiv-2502-21242.description: Abstract In team sports analytics, long-term player tracking remains a challenging task due to player appearance similarity, occlusion, and dynamic motion patterns. Accurately re-identifying players and reconnecting tracklets after extended absences from the field of view or prolonged occlusions is crucial for robust analysis.

arxiv-2503-03953.title: GeoDEN: A Visual Exploration Tool for Analysing the Geographic Spread of Dengue Serotypes
arxiv-2503-03953.creator: A. Marler 1 , Y. Roell 2 , S. Knoblauch 3 , J.P. Messina 4 , T. Jaenisch 2,5 , M. Karimzadeh 1 1 University of Colorado Boulder, 2 Colorado School of Public Health, Center for Global Health, 3 Heidelberg University, 4 University of Oxford, 5 Heidelberg Institute of Global Health (HIGH), Heidelberg U
arxiv-2503-03953.description: Abstract Static maps and animations remain popular in spatial epidemiology of dengue, limiting the analytical depth and scope of visualisations. Over half of the global population live in dengue endemic regions. Understanding the spatiotemporal dynamics of the four closely related dengue serotypes, and their immunological interactions, remains a challenge at a global scale.

BackgroundAlthough prognostic factors associated with mortality in patients with emergency colorectal surgery have been identified, an accurate mortality risk assessment is still necessary to determine the range of therapeutic resources in accordance with the severity of patients.

pmc-10648967.title: Tiliroside Protects against Lipopolysaccharide-Induced Acute Kidney Injury via Intrarenal Renin–Angiotensin System in Mice
pmc-10648967.creator: Xiaoli Yi, Chuanming Xu, Jing Yang, Chao Zhong, Huiru Yang, Le Tang, Shanshan Song, Jun Yu, Marie-Laure Fauconnier
pmc-10648967.description: Tiliroside, a natural flavonoid, has various biological activities and improves several inflammatory diseases in rodents. However, the effect of Tiliroside on lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced acute kidney injury (AKI) and the underlying mechanisms are still unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the potential renoprotective effect of Tiliroside on LPS-induced AKI in mice.

pmc-12812335.title: Maternal Retroperitoneal Cystic Lymphangioma During Pregnancy
pmc-12812335.creator: Marta Campos, Marta Xavier, Mónica Melo, Susana Graça, Claudina Carvalho
pmc-12812335.description: Retroperitoneal cystic lymphangiomas are rare benign tumors, and their occurrence during pregnancy is exceptionally uncommon. We describe a case of a 31-year-old patient at 36 weeks of pregnancy with a large retroperitoneal tumor discovered incidentally during routine obstetric ultrasound (US). One week later, at 37 weeks of gestation, she delivered a healthy newborn via cesarean section.

pmc-12882510.title: Diagnosis of EBV and HCMV infections in pediatric heart transplant recipients
pmc-12882510.creator: Fatemeh Gabeleh, Mohammad Mahdavi, Mohammad Hadi Karbalaie Niya, Mehrdad Ravanshad
pmc-12882510.description: BackgroundViral infections, including human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) and Epstein–Barr Virus (EBV), are significant agents that can cause serious complications and death in heart transplant recipients. This study aims to detect CMV and EBV infections in pediatric heart transplant recipients.MethodsWe conducted a cross-sectional study involving 28 hospitalized children who were candidates for heart transplantation.

pmc-13208641.title: Angle-Resolved Enhancement of Rh800 Dye Photoluminescence Using Plasmonic Metal Gratings
pmc-13208641.creator: Aibibula Abudula, Paiziliya Maitiaximu
pmc-13208641.description: HighlightsPlasmonic metal gratings enhance Rh800 dye photoluminescence by 22-fold through resonant mode matching.FDTD simulations reveal hybrid plasmon-waveguide modes that confine the electric field at the PMMA-air interface.Angle-resolved spectroscopy enables quantitative assessment of PL enhancement across distinct excitation–collection configurations.Shallow grating geometry balances high enhancement with broad resonance tolerance and reproducibility.Cost-effective holographic lithography fabrication suits scalable biosensing and optoelectronic applications.

pmc-13233140.title: Functioning gonadotroph macroadenoma associated with multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1
pmc-13233140.creator: Carlos Eduardo de Melo Oliveira, Delmar Muniz Lourenço Junior, Teresa Neuma Albuquerque Gomes Nogueira, José Ítalo Soares Mota, Raquel Montenegro, Ana Rosa Pinto Quidute
pmc-13233140.description: We report the case of a 35-year-old woman with clinically and genetically confirmed multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 (MEN1) who presented with abnormal uterine bleeding, hypermenorrhea, menstrual irregularities, and visual field defects. Hormonal evaluation revealed elevated estradiol levels, non-suppressed follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH), suppressed luteinizing hormone (LH), and mild hyperprolactinemia. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a large pituitary macroadenoma.

pmc-13280458.title: Breakthrough Tracheobronchial Aspergillosis Caused by Aspergillus calidoustus and Aspergillus niger in a Lung Transplant Recipient Despite Combined Antifungal Prophylaxis
pmc-13280458.creator: Carlos Enrique Calvache Benavides, Martha Daniela Rodríguez Cárdenas, Sergio Saul Sánchez Salazar, Rogelio de Jesús Treviño Rangel, Adrián Camacho Ortiz, Tun-Chieh Chen

pmc-13315110.title: Numerical competence in peafowl: small quantity discrimination
pmc-13315110.creator: Ming-Ray Liao, Ria Patel, Elizabeth J Connor, Maria Ulloa Yoshikawa, Katelyn N Steakley, Orianis A Moore, Jessica L Yorzinski
pmc-13315110.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The ability to discriminate numbers is widespread across taxonomically diverse animals. Some animals may have evolved enhanced numerical abilities to cope with specific social or ecological challenges. Peafowl (Pavo cristatus) are one example in which enhanced numerical abilities could be useful because peacocks have colorful trains that exhibit many eyespot feathers and females may evaluate the number of eyespot feathers to assess their mates. We therefore tested the numerical discrimination abilities of captive peafowl using a custom touchscreen apparatus.

pmc-13401374.title: Academic Psychological Capital and Mental Health: The Mediating Role of Coping Strategies
pmc-13401374.creator: Chung Ho Chan, Mengying Wang, Qiaoqiao Liang, Henry C Y Ho
pmc-13401374.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAcademic pressure represents a primary source of stress for young people. While psychological capital, encompassing hope, efficacy, resilience, and optimism, benefits working populations, its significance in academic contexts remains less understood, particularly regarding student mental health.

pmc-13466746.title: Efficacy and safety of endoscopic transcecal appendectomy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13466746.creator: Mohammed Y. Youssef, Hazem Abosheaishaa, Mohamed H. Eldesouki, Mohammed Al-Aquily, Muhammad M. Elsharkawy, Ahmed Aref, Layth Alzubaidy, Wael T. Mohamed, Mohamed Othman
pmc-13466746.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAppendiceal orifice polyps are rare with prevalence of 0.08%. Surgical approach is the standard approach. Endoscopic transcecal appendectomy (ETA) has several potential advantages when compared to surgery and an alternative to non-surgical candidates. In this study, we review the efficacy and safety of ETA for the management of appendiceal lesionsMethodsA systematic literature search was conducted across MEDLINE/PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane databases. Three studies were included.

pmc-13501575.title: Young adults’ perceptions and experiences in using mobile apps and wearables for health: a qualitative study with public involvement
pmc-13501575.creator: Gaia Leuzzi, Benedetto Giardulli, Mirko Job, Stella Leuzzi, Aldo Scafoglieri, Marco Testa
pmc-13501575.description: BackgroundUnderstanding how young people interact with health apps and wearables might help develop innovative strategies to support health management and improvement adopting a technology they are already familiar with. This study aimed to investigating the user experience of young adults who use apps or wearables for health purposes.MethodsA qualitative study using focus groups was conducted.
